pr_title: [Blazor] Improvements to the interaction between SSR and interactive rendering
pr_body:
# Improvements to the interaction between SSR and interactive rendering

Makes the following improvements to how SSR and interactive rendering interact:
- [X] Detect and initialize interactive root components added via an SSR update
- [X] Cleanly synchronize SSR updates with existing interactive components
  - [X] Updated parameter values get supplied
  - [X] Components get disposed when removed from the DOM

Fixes #48763
Fixes #48764
pr_comments: Also TODO is writing thorough E2E tests that capture all the edge cases. I've updated the test app to demonstrate a mainstream scenario, but there are a lot of intricacies that still need validation.
I've added quite a few tests now and updated the marker key generation per the discussion in this PR.

Thanks for all the helpful feedback, @SteveSandersonMS and @javiercn.

Some follow-up items for RC1:
* Review the strategy we use to ensure clients are well-behaved when adding interactive root components
* Determine if we can simplify the DomSync algorithm to not care about the existence of logical elements. Or, if it does have to, use different layering to separate out logic specific to component comments and logical elements.

issue_context.title: Don't break interactive components when their parent static content is updated
issue_context.body:
When streaming SSR, progressively-enhanced navigation, or progressively-enhanced form posts update part of the DOM dynamically, we have to make sure they behave sensibly when part of that DOM structure is an interactive component.

 * Min bar: destroy the old interactive component and activate a new one
 * Better: preserve the old interactive component, but ignore any new params supplied by the updated static content
 * Best: ... also pass in new params from the updated static content

We likely only have capacity for a relatively basic implementation here, so may be limited to the min bar.

review_comments: If we wanted to, we could also unify the existing `TryDeserializeComponentDescriptorCollection` method with the new `TryDeserializeSinglecomponetnDescriptor` implementation, but that would slightly relax its existing rules and make it less efficient. So, I don't think there's an advantage to doing that at this time.

Is `TryDeserializeComponentDescriptorCollection` only used for older-style Blazor Server apps, not ones rendered using the new EndpointHtmlRenderer?

If so, I personally wouldn't mind if we compromised the efficiency of the older implementation a little for the payoff of not maintaining two different implementations.

But I don't feel strongly and am happy with it staying as you have here if you prefer that.

Yes, it's only used for older Blazor Server apps, where prerendered root components are activated all at once on app startup, then never again.

I think I'll opt to keep it the way it is now, if that's fine with you. We could definitely follow-up and unify these implementations, but for now I want to minimize the risk this PR introduces to existing apps.
Just to be sure, we've definitely been through DataProtection checks before we get here, right? We definitely need not to let clients supply arbitrary parameters or arbitrary component IDs.
Yes, that happens in the call to `TryDeserializeSingleComponentDescriptor`.

Would it also work to add a test here showing the server won't let you add *too many* root components without disposing old ones? Not sure if that enforcement happens within the relevant layer for this unit test though.
`return` probably not needed, though unsure if you're adding this intentionally as a matter of code style ahead of local functions.
This was intentional to make it clear that there isn't some code hiding after the local function declarations. I can remove it if you feel that it adds more confusion than it eliminates!
Maybe you can consider not putting these local functions if their "combined size" is so big that makes you lose track of what's going on in the method. They might be better off as separate members.

Is this based on the expectation that:

 * All these messages are arriving on the same WebSocket connection
 * Messages on a WebSocket connection are guaranteed to be delivered in order of dispatch
 * The client would never ask to activate a component from an older version of the statically-rendered HTML after it receives a new version of the statically-rendered HTML

Or does this miss any scenarios?

Yes, it's based on all of those expectations. For that third one, I couldn't think of a scenario that would contradict that assumption.

If we're worried about these expectations not holding up, we could take an alternate approach where we store a hash set of some invocation ID/sequence pair, and we wouldn't have to make any of the above assumptions. The current assumptions only allow us to stop tracking information about SSR output that we know isn't supposed to be relevant anymore.
